posts.title: Four Years at a Corner Table: The Making of Small Hours
posts.excerpt: Editor Tomas Reyes reflects on the four-year writing process, bilingual book design, and careful production behind Clara Hsu's new essay collection.
posts.content:
In the early autumn of 2022, Clara Hsu began sitting at the same small corner table of a neighborhood café in Da'an District, Taipei. Arriving just past dawn with a fountain pen and a lined notebook, she watched the streetlamps turn off and the morning traffic gather along the avenue. Over the next four years, that single marble surface became the anchor for twenty-one essays examining the overlooked quietude of contemporary city life. Now, Fumi Press is preparing to publish the completed collection, Small Hours: Essays from a Corner Table, on 18 March 2027.

Our partnership with Clara Hsu dates back almost a decade. Founded in 2014 as an independent publisher dedicated to the personal essay, Fumi Press first worked with Hsu on her debut collection, Window Seat, published in 2018. Born in 1986 in Kaohsiung, Hsu has long cultivated a voice rooted in patient observation. Rather than chasing dramatic events or commentary, her work turns toward ordinary moments: the clatter of roll-up metal shutters, the steam rising from an early coffee, and the quiet movement of rain across tiled rooftops. In Small Hours, that focus is deepened across 248 carefully calibrated pages.

Bringing this book into the world required an equally deliberate material approach. Book designer Noor Haddad established a 14 × 21 cm format, balancing generous margins with clean typography that honors the contemplative nature of the prose. Documentary photographer Jun Park spent weeks recording early morning light and street scenes with 35mm film grain, creating images that accompany the volume without illustrating it literally. Moreover, Small Hours is published simultaneously in English and Traditional Chinese on the same day, reflecting Hsu's bilingual readership and our commitment to cross-linguistic literature.

To honor the craft behind the collection, we are producing a signed first printing limited to 1,500 numbered hardcover copies, priced at USD 34. Alongside the hardcover, we have prepared English and Traditional Chinese paperbacks at USD 22, a DRM-free bilingual EPUB at USD 12, an unabridged author-read audiobook running 6 hours and 40 minutes at USD 18, and a launch bundle at USD 58. For reading groups, our book-club pack provides six paperbacks and a discussion guide for USD 110. Pre-orders close on 10 March 2027, with signed copies shipping worldwide from Taipei on 11 March 2027.

Following publication, Clara Hsu will embark on a four-city launch tour, with readings beginning at 19:30 local time. The tour visits Taipei at The Corner Room in Da'an on 20 March with bookseller Mina Cho, Tokyo at Annex Reading Room in Kiyosumi on 27 March, Paris at Librairie du Quai Bas on 3 April, and Berlin at Lesesaal Nord on 10 April with Hanna Weber. Each reading is free but strictly capped at 60 seats to preserve an intimate environment. Early readers like teacher Rafael Ortiz have remarked on how these essays slow down our perception of the everyday. As we finalize press sheets in Taipei, we look forward to placing this volume into your hands.
